# AIPerf — Python orchestrator + native runner session-bootstrap index

Single-page topology of the important source + design files, with a one-line
purpose for each, so an agent knows which file to open for a given question.

## Product entry point and architecture

- **Native binary:** the human-facing `aiperf` command is a native Rust binary
  (crate `aiperf-cli`) — it owns `profile`/`config` natively
  (byte-exact Config v2), projects one protocol-v2 request, and drives execution
  by re-execing ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`), delegating only peripheral subcommands
  (`plot`/`service`/`plugins`) to Python (embedded CPython, or `python -m aiperf`
  in the lean build).
  Config v2's schema, planning, outer loops, and presentation stay Python-defined.
  The one `aiperf` binary is BOTH the entry point AND the execution engine — the sole
  executable that dispatches load and owns exactly one benchmark hot path (no separate
  runner binary). The runtime library it links is crate `aiperf-runtime` (`rust/runtime`).
  The standalone `aiperf-mock-server`
  developer/test target is an ordinary online inference server, not an
  orchestrated backend process. `rust/runtime` is a runtime library and
  intentionally has no binary target (the native binary is the `aiperf-cli` crate).
- **Source organization:** Rust execution truth is `rust/`; Python frontend
  truth includes `src/aiperf/config`, `src/aiperf/orchestrator`, and
  `src/aiperf/cli_runner`. The old controller/service/ZMQ implementation under
  `src/` remains legacy and is not an alternate hot path.
- **Agent instructions:** `CLAUDE.md` = `AGENTS.md` = `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
  = `.cursor/rules/python.mdc` (byte-identical body; keep in sync via
  `python tools/check_agent_files_sync.py`).

## The architecture in one breath

The native `aiperf` binary projects one side-effect-free authored request and
re-execs itself (`aiperf --execute`) to run it; the Python frontend is pure
Python (legacy service mesh only) and does not bridge to Rust — there is no
Python request projection, protocol-v1 resolver, conversion, or fallback. The execution engine exact-image-preflights the requested transport and workload
and direct-loads their registered adapters (any workload runs over any transport;
there is no pair map or compatibility gate). It drives **ONLINE-real** over
native HTTP or gRPC (including KServe OIP, NVIDIA Riva ASR/TTS/NLP, and AWS
SageMaker Runtime `InvokeEndpoint`/`InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream`) and
**ONLINE-mock** over HTTP through one `{transport,
clock}` seam. The base image registers HTTP scheduled/graph/static-accuracy/
agentic and native gRPC scheduled execution. **OFFLINE-mock** is product-
reachable through the same Python Config-v2 path when the runner is built with
the non-default `dynosim` feature; that image adds `dynosim_offline` and
`dynosim_online` scheduled and graph execution. Unregistered transports or
workloads fail closed.
The open `vllm_generate` endpoint is token-native end to end: its descriptor
requires validated raw IDs, `aiperf-dataset` stores them as content-addressed
handles and generates synthetic IDs without decoding text, online HTTP maps
them to `/inference/v1/generate`, and Dynamo-offline resolves the same handle
without constructing a request body or invoking an encoder. Returned ID arrays
remain non-text response data and drive exact token/usage observations.
Verbatim `raw_payload` and `inputs_json` requests remain opaque for ordinary
endpoints: composition preserves exact wire bytes, performs no BPE encoding,
and leaves composed input tokens unset (`None` / JSON `null`). Only endpoints
declaring `requires_raw_token_ids`, including `vllm_generate`, cause authored
`token_ids` to be validated, interned, and counted as `Some(length)`.
Direct Graph-IR currently lacks that linear-dataset handle and fails preparation
for endpoints with the requirement.
Generated image/video delivery can be externalized through one run-owned native
content server. Python projects `AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_*` into a strict v2
sidecar input; `aiperf-dataset` injects inline or file/URL publication; the
runner binds, tracks, and drains `aiperf-content-server`. Audio remains inline.
Scheduled/graph/static-accuracy online HTTP execute the sidecar;
agentic/evaluation, native gRPC, and offline pairs reject it.
Time lives behind `Clock` (`RealClock` vs
integer-ns DES `SimClock`); dispatch lives behind `RequestSink<R>` +
`RequestObserver` into a `TraceCollector`; token callbacks can carry
`ObservedTokenKind::{Output,Reasoning}` and fall back to unclassified `on_token`,
while terminal `ObservedUsage` carries endpoint counts as optional fields.
`is_virtual()` picks the `drive_real`
(reactor) vs `drive_sim` (idle-pump) driver over the *same* executor.
`RequestObserver` is intentionally local-loop (`!Send`/`!Sync`) so returned-event
fan-out and collection use `Rc`/`RefCell` without per-token locks. Thread-per-core,
`Rc`/`RefCell`, `!Send`, `spawn_local` on the hot path.

Offline/online Dynamo replay is authored through `aiperf profile` as Config-v2
transports (`transport.type: dynosim_offline` / `dynosim_online`), not a
separate command. The typed `DynosimTransportConfig`
(`src/aiperf/config/dynosim.py`) mirrors the runner's `DynosimTransportSpec` and
projects verbatim into the protocol-v2 request; trace and concurrency reuse the
shared `dataset`/`phases` surface. There is no `replay_mode` field. The live
Dynamo mocker server and the replay-optimize sweep remain native
`python -m dynamo.*` tools.

Native recorded-graph compilation is built for recursive WEKA objects and
`dynamo.request.trace.v1` JSONL/gzip/segmented captures. Both enter one
runner-owned graph-input resolver, share one LCP-trie lowerer, and produce dense
segments plus Graph-IR without a Python trace data plane. Content synthesis uses
the existing `aiperf-rng` BLAKE3/PCG64 stream only; there is no Python SHA/MT
duplicate. Equivalent logical WEKA and Dynamo inputs produce byte-identical
native segments and HTTP bodies under that canonical stream.

## Crate topology (`rust/`)

| Crate | Read for | Entry files |
|---|---|---|
| `aiperf-runtime` (`rust/runtime`, library-only — no binary) | the whole native runtime the `aiperf` binary links: the `{clock}` seam, prepared HTTP/gRPC sinks, online paced/scheduled/adaptive/static-accuracy paths, the provider-neutral evaluation workload/host registry/arbiter/ledger/report join, legacy stateful agentic seams, datasets/segments, the metrics engine, the Graph-IR runtime, telemetry side-channels, and the native export plane. Owns the single `AIPerfRegistry`/`AIPerfExtension` composition seam (`extensions/`) and, behind the `engine` Cargo feature that ONLY `aiperf-cli` enables, hosts the relocated v2 layer `aiperf_runtime::engine` (protocol/registry, execution factories and drivers, coordinator, `Application`, cellular controller/cell, control-plane HTTP, GPU/network/server side-channels). Sixteen former `aiperf-*` library crates are now its `aiperf_runtime::<module>` modules | `src/lib.rs`, `extensions/`, `engine/`, `transport/http/sink.rs`, `transport/grpc/sink.rs`, `run.rs`, `scheduled.rs`, `phase_runtime.rs`, `evaluation.rs`, `metrics.rs`, `report.rs`, and the module dirs (`clock/`, `rng/`, `timing/`, `dataset/`, `endpoints/`, `graph/`, `metrics_core/`, `adaptive_core/`, `accuracy_core/`, `transport/` (`core`/`http`/`grpc`), `content_server/`, `gpu_telemetry/`, `server_metrics/`, `network_latency/`) |
| `aiperf-mock-server` | standalone online test/benchmark inference target: OpenAI chat/completions/embeddings, TGI, rerank, image, multimodal, and RAG routes; real SSE; analytic/batch-scheduler latency; deterministic token generation; prefix-cache policy; Prometheus dialects; and synthetic DCGM telemetry. Optional `--grpc-port` adds a KServe OIP v2 `GRPCInferenceService` (`ModelInfer`/`ModelStreamInfer`/`ModelReady`/`ServerLive`/`ServerReady`) over h2c, reusing the same generation seam and the `aiperf_runtime::transport::grpc::proto` prost messages (no build-time protoc); HTTP-only under `--processes N`. An optional `--accuracy-dataset <path>` loads a JSONL `{prompt, ground_truth}` dataset and returns the grader-formatted correct answer for a seeded fraction of matched prompts (`--accuracy-correct-rate`/`--accuracy-format`), with chain-of-thought (`--accuracy-cot-rate`) and parser-choke adversarial shapes (`--accuracy-adversarial-rate`: reasoning-only #1136, `object:null` stream frame #1010, whitespace/case/boxed/conflicting/unicode); ground truth is loaded mock-side and keyed on the prompt (`--accuracy-match` exact/substring/`_ci` modes + per-row `match_key`; never sent over the wire). A live `GET /accuracy` endpoint plus `aiperf_mock_accuracy_*` Prometheus metrics report the run's actual served correct/matched tally. Also closes runner-to-mock e2e gaps (each raw-export tested): configurable error injection (status menu/Retry-After/mid-stream SSE), extended `--usage-*` accounting, `tool_calls` emission, `/v1/responses` + `/inference/v1/generate` + `/openai/v1/*` + KServe HTTP v2/v1 routes, gRPC KServe rankings/images/VLM tensors (`--grpc-behavior`), Riva ASR/TTS/NLP gRPC, AWS SageMaker Runtime `/endpoints/{model}/invocations` and `/endpoints/{model}/invocations-response-stream` routes (the latter framed as real AWS `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` binary frames, verified wire-compatible against a genuine `boto3` `sagemaker-runtime` client), `--uds` Unix-socket listener, and TLS/`grpcs` (`--tls-*`). Exports both a test router and a tuned Hyper server binary; not a runner dependency | `src/app.rs`, `src/grpc.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/handlers.rs`, `src/tokens.rs`, `src/latency.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`, `src/prefix_cache.rs`, `src/metrics.rs`, `src/prom.rs`, `src/dcgm.rs`, `src/accuracy.rs`, `src/grpc_riva.rs`, `src/tls.rs`, `src/main.rs` |
| `aiperf-cli` (binary `aiperf`) | native Rust entry point (crate `aiperf-cli`, lib + bin) that owns `aiperf profile` (single run **and** grid/zip sweeps) and `aiperf config init/validate/expand` — no Python on the profile/config path: clap flags + serde Config v2 projected onto the `protocol_v2` schema, re-execing ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`) once per sweep cell, aggregated into `sweep_aggregate/`, with the console summary echoed to the terminal. It is BOTH the entry point AND the execution engine (no separate runner binary; capabilities is the in-process `execute_mode::capabilities_catalog` fn). Comma-list flags expand natively (`sweep/`, alpha-sorted axes, byte-exact per-cell requests, artifact-dir 5-row table, `base+idx` seeds); `--num-profile-runs N` adds N trials per variation (byte-exact dirs/seeds). Single-trial sweeps write a byte-exact `sweep_aggregate/profile_export_aiperf_sweep.{json,csv}`; multi-trial confidence aggregate deferred (scipy t-dist). `config init` scaffolds 28 embedded templates; `config validate` applies `${ENV}` + Jinja2 expansion (`expand.rs`), inline dataset `records:`, and the distribution discriminator; a config `sweep:` block (grid/zip dotted-path axes, `sweep/yaml_sweep.rs`) expands natively and previews via `config expand`. Native profile/config byte-exact vs Python for every modeled flag (all GenAI-Perf aliases; zero pure-alias gaps; scenario/trajectory/unsafe/agentic + always-emitted accuracy/endpoint_profiles/failure_policy land natively). NEVER shells to the Python profile command — request projection is native for every modeled flag (media/rankings/synthesis/scenario/dataset-filter/search all golden-verified); accuracy execution uses the pinned Python evaluators (sanctioned in-process/subprocess path), never the Python profile command. The adaptive **SLA-search** subsystem is built: all four `max-concurrency-under-sla --search-style` styles run natively as dynamic ask-tell loops (one `aiperf --execute` child per probe, SLA metric read from `native-v2.json`) — `monotonic` pure-Rust; default `smooth_isotonic` (scipy PAVA+PCHIP), `bo` (BoTorchSampler+qLogNEI), `optuna` (TPE/GP) behind the opt-in `search-pyo3` feature (embeds CPython; default binary stays Python-free). Peripheral subcommands native pure-Rust (no pyo3): `analyze-trace`, `validate mooncake-trace`, `speed-bench-report`, `chat` (hyper streaming client + stats), `synthesize agentic-code` (seeded dataset generator on the byte-exact numpy `Generator` port `aiperf_runtime::rng::numpy_generator`) — all byte-exact vs Python — plus `compare`, a native-only side-by-side diff of two `profile_export_aiperf.json` summaries (per-metric delta/percent + better/worse verdict from the catalog `PlotMetricDirection`; no Python counterpart). Heavier subcommands (plot=matplotlib, service=legacy mesh, plugins) run in-process via embedded CPython in the `pyo3-embed`/`search-pyo3` build (zero subprocess), else a `python -m aiperf` subprocess in the lean build. Parity: `tools/parity/` (`dump_golden.py` single-run, `dump_sweep.py`, `dump_sweep_aggregate.py`, and dynamic-search `dump_monotonic.py`/`dump_isotonic.py`/`dump_bayes.py` byte-exact on pure-Rust+seeded-TPE) | `rust/cli/src/{main.rs,lib.rs,dispatch.rs,delegate.rs,profile.rs,flags.rs,load.rs,yaml.rs,execute.rs,exec_bin.rs,execute_mode.rs,render.rs,search.rs,isotonic.rs,bayes.rs,pyfit.rs,pyopt.rs,compare.rs}`, `rust/cli/src/{sweep,config}/`, `mimalloc_options.c`/`build.rs` |
| `pyext` (module `aiperf._native`, `rust/pyext`) | packaging-only pyo3 `cdylib`: maturin's compiled target (`aiperf._native`) alongside the packaged `src/aiperf` frontend (`python-source = "src"`). It does NOT build the unified `aiperf` binary — `tools/wheel_repack.py` (run by `make wheel`) repacks that binary directly into the wheel's scripts directory as `aiperf-<ver>.data/scripts/aiperf`, so the installed `aiperf` command IS the native binary (there is no `[project.scripts] aiperf` console-script entry; the pure-Python app is reachable as `aiperf-python` = `aiperf.entrypoint:main`, and `python -m aiperf`). No internal deps; carries only `aiperf --version` build metadata; never imported at runtime | `rust/pyext/Cargo.toml`, `rust/pyext/src/lib.rs` |
| `aiperf-e2e-tests` (`rust/e2e-tests`) | the end-to-end harness: drives the Python `aiperf profile` entry point against `aiperf-mock-server` and verifies the raw per-record JSONL (`profile_export_raw.jsonl`) for timing + data. Builds without the `engine` layer | `rust/e2e-tests/tests/`, `rust/e2e-tests/tests/common/` |

The five workspace crates are `aiperf-runtime`, `aiperf-cli`, `aiperf-mock-server`, `pyext`, and `aiperf-e2e-tests`. Fifteen former `aiperf-*` library crates are now modules of `aiperf-runtime` (`aiperf_runtime::<m>`): `clock`, `rng`, `metrics_core`, `timing`, `adaptive_core`, `accuracy_core`, `endpoints`, `dataset`, `content_server`, `extensions`, `transport` (with `transport::core` vocabulary + `transport::http`/`transport::grpc` wire impls), `graph`, `gpu_telemetry`, `server_metrics`, `network_latency`, plus `dispatch` (from the retired `loadgen-core` crate, never one of the sixteen `aiperf-*` crates) and the feature-gated `engine`. Per-module purpose + key files: [`docs/module-organization.md`](docs/module-organization.md).

Deps: `aiperf-cli` → {`aiperf-runtime` (with the `engine` feature)} and re-execs ITSELF (`aiperf --execute`) at runtime (a launched process, not a second binary); `aiperf-runtime` → optional `dynamo-mocker` only under `dynosim`; `aiperf-mock-server` → {`aiperf-runtime`}; `pyext` → {`pyo3`} only (no internal deps, nothing depends on it). Within `aiperf-runtime` the modules compose through `crate::<module>::` imports: `metrics_core` stays IO-free and runtime-neutral, and the `gpu_telemetry`/`server_metrics`/`network_latency` telemetry producers feed the shared side-channel accumulator seam without core metrics ever depending back on a producer. `aiperf-cli` and `aiperf-mock-server` do not depend on each other; real-network tests spawn the mock binary as an ordinary target.

## Run AIPerf

```bash
# Generate, validate, and run through the only user-facing entry point.
aiperf config init --template minimal --output benchmark.yaml
aiperf config validate benchmark.yaml
aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml

# Externalize generated images/videos through the run-owned native server.
mkdir -p /tmp/aiperf-content
AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_ENABLED=true \
  AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_CONTENT_DIR=/tmp/aiperf-content \
  aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml

# Cellular (multi-process) mode: `--cells N` (or `runtime.cells: N`) makes the launched
# aiperf a controller that spawns N `aiperf --cell` children over a
# (cell_id, cell_count) budget partition and merges their records into one report.
# `--cells 1` (default) is the unchanged single-process path. Supported for synthetic,
# single-turn runs over the http OR grpc transport with request-bounded phases (gRPC runs
# the SAME cell executor as http — the cell issuer + records shipper live above the
# transport); a run seed and single URL are NOT required (seedless auto-derives a shared
# seed, multi-URL round-robins cell-locally, ramps/rate/cancellation aggregate-equivalent,
# warned). Graph programs (dag_jsonl/weka_trace/dynamo_trace) also partition across cells
# (trace-level, concatenation-merged; a --sketch-metrics graph cell ships a folded sketch
# store, merged like exact-fold). Fails closed on the dynosim offline/online transport +
# scheduled duration/adaptive. E2e: test_cellular.rs + test_grpc_cellular.rs (scheduled) +
# test_graph_cellular.rs (incl. sketch store-ship).
aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml --cells 4

# Developer-only runner protocol inventory; normal runs are launched by Python.
# capabilities: aiperf_cli::execute_mode::capabilities_catalog (in-process; no --capabilities argv mode)
```

`cargo run -p aiperf-runtime` is intentionally invalid: the `aiperf-runtime` Rust
package has no binary. Config-v2 YAML expresses endpoints, datasets, phases, ramps,
cancellation, adaptive policy, static/stateful accuracy, provider-neutral
evaluation, telemetry, artifacts, and open
transport/workload selections. Python expands outer loops; execution retains the
side-effect-free authored-v2 shape through validation and execution. It
requires the selected runner image to advertise the exact pair and never
resolves or converts the run to protocol v1. Explicit open workloads delegate
phase-stop semantics to their registered Rust factory; implicit built-in
workloads retain Python's generic stop validation. `dag_jsonl`, `weka_trace`,
and `dynamo_trace` enter the runner-owned Graph-IR input adapter once and invoke
exactly one selected compiler, lowering directly to graph plans plus one frozen
segment store without a second registry or linear dataset intermediate.
Recorded formats accept `synthesis.max_osl`, `max_context_length`,
`idle_gap_cap_seconds`, and `allow_dataset_wrap` where applicable; synthetic
and count/hash-based trace prompt synthesis share `prompts.corpus` /
`--prompt-corpus` over `sonnet`, `coding`, and tokenizer-driven `random`,
defaulting to `coding` for recorded-graph reconstruction;
Python forwards those authored values without parsing trace payloads. Native gRPC requires
`transport.type: grpc` with `grpc://` or `grpcs://` URLs, behind the default-on
`grpc` Cargo feature (a lean HTTP-only build drops it and `tonic`); offline/wall-clock
in-process Dynamo replay requires `transport.type: dynosim_offline` or
`transport.type: dynosim_online` and a feature-bearing runner. Each native
transport (`http`/`grpc`/`dry_run`) is resolved from the transport registry
through its `NativeTransportExecution` binding, so the scheduled/graph workloads
never branch on a transport enum. There is ONE thread-per-core execution model:
`workers==1` runs a single co-located `WorkerSink` on the coordinator reactor
(`turn_execution::build_native`), and `workers>1` runs under a `runtime.dispatch`
selector (`sharded` | `global` | `global-hop`; `global` is the default — see
`docs/specs/global-exact-dispatch.md`): `sharded` tiles that same sink across `W`
self-contained sub-cells with no cross-thread per-request hop
(`sharded_scheduled::run_sharded_scheduled`); `global` keeps that same tiling but
admits concurrency/rate from a shared per-cell gate for byte-exact aggregate
parity; `global-hop` revives a cross-thread per-request hop dispatcher
(`turn_execution::ThreadPerCoreExecutor`, `global_hop::run_global_hop`) for exact
global issuance order. Every workload shape shards (rate/concurrency by budget
under `sharded`/by shared gate under `global`, user_centric/fixed_schedule per
conversation, static-accuracy by per-shard capture graded once at finalize;
`shardable` is just `workers > 1`). A transport contributes only a
`WorkerSink` via an `ExecutionSinkBuilder`, never its own worker loop/measurement
(`transport::reduce`/`transport::measure` are shared) — gRPC has no parallel
execution path. Adding a transport is writing a sink builder and registering a
factory; gating one out is not registering it.

Provider-neutral evaluation additionally requires the selected runner
deployment's wheel-`RECORD`-verified companion roots or generated adjacent
root-registry sidecar. Missing or drifted roots make the evaluator distributions
unavailable and omit `http + evaluation`; Python does not substitute an
ambient provider environment or a legacy workload.

Content-server validation is side-effect-free. Image/video URL publication
requires both `AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_ENABLED=true` and a non-empty existing
`AIPERF_CONTENT_SERVER_CONTENT_DIR`; enabled with an empty directory starts a
temporary server but keeps media inline. See `docs/tutorials/content-server.md`.

`AIPERF_RNG_BACKEND=rust` (default `python`) swaps the seeded random
substrate from Python's Mersenne Twister + NumPy (SHA-256 derivation) to a
pure-Python byte-exact implementation of the Rust `aiperf_runtime::rng` `Pcg64` + BLAKE3 substrate
(`src/aiperf/common/rng_parity/`), so seeded Python and Rust produce identical
streams in tests. `Environment.RNG.BACKEND` in `src/aiperf/common/environment.py`;
parity is proved against committed Rust golden vectors
(`rust/runtime/examples/rng_parity_vectors.rs` ->
`rust/runtime/tests/data/rng_parity_vectors.json`).

The online concurrency and request-rate issuers own all applicable live ramp
actuators. User-centric owns only its optional session-concurrency pool, while
fixed schedule owns none; unsupported ramps fail validation rather than becoming
inert. Scheduled strategies support per-turn cancellation and turn-zero sticky
endpoint routing.

## Canonical static accuracy

Static accuracy is configured through Config v2 and launched by
`aiperf profile --config ...`. Python selects the pinned evaluator environment;
the runner supervises it while retaining all inference traffic and timing.

Rust sends every LLM request and parses every response through its normal
transport. The Python/Lighteval child prepares opaque problems and batch-grades
terminal response text; it never contacts the inference server, and ground
truth/private tests never cross the JSONL protocol. The evaluator protocol rejects
unknown static-response fields and restricts static prompts to `{role, content}`; stateful
agent/tool messages retain role-specific fields losslessly. The worker redirects
ambient fd 1 output to stderr and native v2 records its source/lock identity.

## Stateful agentic accuracy

The Harbor, AgentLab/BrowserGym, and MCPMark providers and Rust
`AgenticWorkload` are product-reachable through the registered
`http + agentic` protocol-v2 pair. Real subprocess proofs cover the
supervised evaluator, authenticated callback gateway, ordinary Rust HTTP/SSE
dispatch, and scored native-v2 report. Do not add a second CLI or move model
traffic into Python.

Harbor owns task packages, Terminus-2, environments, trajectories, terminal
execution, and verifier rewards. Primary calls use its queue callback. Packaged
LLM-backed environments/verifiers receive an authenticated callback address;
Rust's ingress converts those calls to the same scheduled workload and never
forwards directly. Rust issues every turn through the generic online
scheduled/transport runner. Native v2 records exact worker/lock/container,
harness source/version, dataset revision, agent, environment, verifier, authored
configuration, canonical rewards, episode records, and artifacts. Infrastructure
and cancellation records are never converted into zero/incorrect scores.
Harbor's canonical source forms are accepted unchanged: Hub
`org/name@ref`, legacy `name@version` (for example `bfcl@1.0`), and an existing
local task-directory path. Hub tags are reported as resolved content hashes;
legacy versions are frozen before Harbor enumerates their tasks.

The removed native-CLI route remains deleted; product proofs launch only the
strict runner through Python's Config-v2 path.

AgentLab 0.4.2 plus BrowserGym 0.14.3 is the canonical browser provider. It
directly runs `DEFAULT_BENCHMARKS`, `GenericAgent`, and `ExpArgs`; its sync model
callback emits JSONL and only a Rust terminal result can resume the browser
loop. BrowserGym owns prompts, actions, Playwright transitions, traces, and
rewards. Browser tasks use dependency-safe sequential admission. The separately
hashed worker lock is required because AgentLab's OpenAI <2 constraint conflicts
with Harbor's LiteLLM/OpenAI 2.x constraint.

MCPMark commit `cd45b7f57923b9b3985467f5139927575f83141c` is a third
independently hash-locked provider. MCPMark owns the registry, task instructions,
100-turn loop, MCP servers, state managers, task-local `verify.py`, artifacts,
and cleanup. AIPerf replaces only `litellm.acompletion` with its JSONL broker;
Python never receives a model-server URL. Native v2 records MCPMark's exact
source/lock, canonical agent controls, selected server artifact, task digest,
and concrete local-environment digest.

## Run the scheduled workloads

Request-rate, concurrency, user-centric, and fixed-schedule strategies are
Config-v2 phase variants executed by the runner. See
`src/aiperf/config/templates/{latency_test,multi_turn_conversation,fixed_schedule}.yaml`
for runnable examples.

Fixed-trace zero/window policy is expressed in the Config-v2 fixed-schedule
phase. Rust records scheduled, issued, dispatch, first-token, TTFT, terminal,
and aggregate lateness facts in the native result/artifacts selected by Python.

## AIPerf offline engine

The Dynamo native crates come from the pinned ai-dynamo/dynamo git dep (see
`rust/runtime/Cargo.toml`; no sibling checkout). Library developers can compile
the adapter; `dynamo-full` enables every optional mocker family (run cargo from
the `rust/` workspace dir):

```bash
cd rust
cargo build -p aiperf-runtime --features dynosim
cargo test -p aiperf-runtime --features dynosim --lib
cargo build -p aiperf-cli --features dynosim
```

There is no native `--offline` CLI. An `aiperf` binary built with `dynosim`
registers `dynosim + scheduled` and `dynosim + graph`; Python
authors the same Config-v2 request and exact-image preflight rejects a base
runner that does not advertise those pairs.

Single, aggregate, and disaggregate topologies, both routers, all five trace
formats, cancellation, ramps, adaptive controls, SLA goodput, and raw/timed
artifacts run on one `SimClock` with no inference server. Before any offline API
returns, the complete common flat reports must serialize to identical compact
JSON bytes: 74 base fields, plus three goodput fields when configured. Multi-
phase runs retain the independent compatibility observer; single-phase product
runs avoid that duplicate row store and reconstruct the byte-equal compatibility
report from Dynamo after drain while native metrics remain callback-driven.
Requested KV offload fails closed on initialization error. Canonical accuracy
alone remains online because the timing engine does not generate semantic answer
text.

## Run offline/online Dynamo replay through `aiperf profile`

```bash
# transport.type: dynosim_offline|dynosim_online; offline is byte-exact with native replay.
aiperf profile --config dynosim_offline_replay.yaml
```

This requires an `aiperf` binary (crate `aiperf-cli`) built with the `dynosim` Cargo feature (which
pulls the pinned ai-dynamo/dynamo git dep). There is no `replay_mode` field; the
transport ID selects virtual or wall-clock replay. The live Dynamo mocker server and the
replay-optimize sweep remain native tools: `python -m dynamo.mocker` and Dynamo's
profiler.

## "Which file answers…" quick map

- **How is virtual time deterministic?** `rust/runtime/src/clock/sim_clock.rs`
  (min-heap, `(at_ns, seq_no)`, `advance_to`) + `rust/runtime/src/graph/runtime.rs`
  (`drive_sim` and `drive_sim_with_source` idle-pumps).
- **How is a request dispatched + measured?** `rust/runtime/src/dispatch/sink.rs` (traits)
  → `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` (`TransportSink`) →
  `rust/runtime/src/dispatch/observer.rs` (`CollectorObserver`).
- **Where is evaluator ownership split?** Provider-neutral control/isolation lives
  in `rust/runtime/src/accuracy_core/{provider,provider_protocol,supervisor,isolation,artifacts}.rs`;
  Rust-owned host effects, admission, ledger, proxy, sealing, and report join live
  in `rust/runtime/src/evaluation{.rs,/}`; the provider-neutral host seam lives under
  `src/aiperf/accuracy/evaluation/`. Legacy static/stateful ownership remains in
  `rust/runtime/src/accuracy_core/{protocol,worker}.rs`,
  `src/aiperf/accuracy/{worker,agentic,model_broker,harbor,harbor_agent,browsergym,mcpmark}.py`,
  `rust/runtime/src/{accuracy,agentic,agentic_gateway}.rs`, and
  `rust/runtime/src/engine/agentic_execution.rs` until its exact deletion gates pass.
- **Where do native TTFT/ITL/e2e/throughput/goodput and sweeps come from?**
  `rust/runtime/src/metrics.rs` (runtime join) → `rust/runtime/src/metrics_core/{store,accumulator,sweepline}.rs`.
  `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` also translates the real transport trace into HTTP metric facts;
  `rust/runtime/src/dispatch/collector.rs` remains the compact compatibility summary.
- **Where are streamed chunks and usage parsed?** `rust/runtime/src/endpoints/chat_chunk.rs`
  (`ChatChunk`, `Usage`) + `rust/runtime/src/dispatch/observer.rs` (delta-token recorder).
  `rust/runtime/src/http.rs` emits terminal usage and `metrics_core` reconciles
  collector-wide completion counts while retaining observed chunk timings.
- **How does the online loop work?** `rust/runtime/src/run.rs` (Clock-paced arrival
  generator, dynamic session/prefill `SlotPool`s, `StopChecker`, adaptive task).
- **How do user-centric and fixed-schedule runs work?**
  `rust/runtime/src/{scheduled,scheduler,user_centric,fixed_schedule,multiturn}.rs`;
  exact virtual-time coverage is in `rust/runtime/tests/scheduled_sim.rs`, and real HTTP
  library timing coverage is in `rust/runtime/tests/scheduled_real_mock.rs`.
- **How does adaptive scale work?** `rust/runtime/src/adaptive_core/{window,sla,step,controller,runtime}.rs`
  (pure control) → `rust/runtime/src/adaptive.rs` (live-actuator assembly) →
  `rust/runtime/src/run.rs` (backend-neutral online/offline issuer integration).
- **Where do ramps, request cancellation, and sticky endpoint selection live?**
  `rust/runtime/src/timing/{ramping,cancellation,url_selection}.rs` (policy traits) →
  `rust/runtime/src/{ancillary,run,scheduled,http}.rs` (issuer/session wiring) →
  `rust/runtime/src/transport/http/{client,transport}/` (send-complete abort).
- **How does authored DAG input reach graph mode directly?**
  `rust/runtime/src/graph/input.rs` (adapter registry + complete-source parse) →
  `lowering.rs` (`GraphTracePlan` + frozen `SegmentStore`, no linear dataset) →
  `workload.rs` / `placement.rs` → `rust/runtime/src/engine/graph_phase_runtime.rs`
  (one lifecycle/policy driver) → `graph_execution.rs` or `offline_execution.rs`
  (injected backend adapter).
  The throughput harness remains `rust/runtime/src/graph/transport_bench.rs`
  (thread-per-core lanes, transport::http, UDS).
- **How are prompts built without re-serializing?** `rust/runtime/src/dataset/segment.rs`
  (blake3 prefix-dependent dense handles) + `materialize.rs` (wire splice).
- **How are generated media files served?**
  `src/aiperf/{common/environment.py,orchestrator/rust_wire.py}` (public settings
  and strict projection) → `rust/runtime/src/dataset/generator/` (publication seam) →
  `rust/runtime/src/content_server/{publisher,server,tracker}.rs` (file URLs, serving,
  tracking) → `rust/runtime/src/engine/{sidecar_input,online_execution,execute}.rs`
  (strict input, pair preparation, run lifecycle).
- **Where is native-v2 JSON built/written?** `rust/runtime/src/metrics_core/report.rs` →
  `rust/runtime/src/report.rs`; strict run selection/composition is in
  `rust/runtime/src/engine/{protocol_v2,registry,execute}.rs`.

## Design specs (`docs/specs/` — intent, code is authoritative)

Full index: [`docs/specs/README.md`](docs/specs/README.md). Each spec states current built
behavior plus, where present, an explicit `Future requirements` section.

Whole system:

- [`docs/specs/architecture.md`](docs/specs/architecture.md) — process model, crate
  topology, and the three orthogonal seams (time, transport, workload).
- [`docs/specs/repository-layout.md`](docs/specs/repository-layout.md) — Cargo workspace
  topology, package identity, and naming rules enforced by
  `tools/check_crate_layout.py`.
- [`docs/specs/wheel-packaging.md`](docs/specs/wheel-packaging.md) — the single
  installable artifact: `bundle-cli` → maturin → `tools/wheel_repack.py`, the
  PEP-427 `.data/scripts/aiperf` binary interface, and the future removal of the
  callerless `rust/pyext` cdylib that pins the wheel to one CPython minor.
- [`docs/specs/extension-registry.md`](docs/specs/extension-registry.md) — the
  `AIPerfRegistry`/`AIPerfExtension` link-time composition seam, its capability
  categories, and the frozen bootstrap object graph.
- [`docs/specs/runner-protocol.md`](docs/specs/runner-protocol.md) — the Config-v2 ↔
  execution boundary: the protocol-v2 stdio envelope, the `BenchmarkRun`
  vocabulary, dataset/transport path selection, and the in-process
  linked-capability catalog.
- [`docs/specs/config-model-unification.md`](docs/specs/config-model-unification.md)
  — planned convergence of the Config-v2 front end onto one typed
  `BenchmarkConfig`/`BenchmarkRun` shared by the CLI producer and runtime consumer
  (mirroring Python's `AIPerfConfig`→`build_benchmark_plan`→`BenchmarkRun`),
  retiring the untyped projection seam and the per-workload `*WorkloadConfigV2` DTOs.
- [`docs/specs/typed-factory-runner.md`](docs/specs/typed-factory-runner.md)
  — planned completion of config-model-unification: the runtime consumes the typed
  `BenchmarkRun` directly and selects a component by an open, normalized string id
  (`RegistryId`) whose config is a typed struct for built-ins and an opaque
  `RawValue` (plugin-decoded) only for the runtime-plugin tail — deleting the
  `AuthoredRunSpecV2` projection; the discriminant stays a string (as Python's
  `ExtensibleStrEnum` is), enums reserved for closed knobs.
- [`docs/specs/2026-07-24-rust-port-flow-deck-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-07-24-rust-port-flow-deck-design.md)
  — design for the `apps/aiperf-flow` `rust-port-flow` deck: an interactive,
  zoomable, playable request-lifecycle explainer of the whole Rust port, plus
  the shared `src/interactive/` primitives it introduces.
- [`docs/specs/2026-07-24-rust-port-flow-v2-swimlane-timeline.md`](docs/specs/2026-07-24-rust-port-flow-v2-swimlane-timeline.md)
  — swimlane-timeline redesign of that deck: the request as one line riding a
  time axis (the Clock seam) through subsystem lanes in nested seam frames;
  supersedes the node-graph rendering, keeps the nine-stage content and the
  `ZoomStage`/`useFlowPlayer`/`SeamToggle` primitives.
- [`docs/specs/2026-07-23-aiperf-flow-elk-layout-engine.md`](docs/specs/2026-07-23-aiperf-flow-elk-layout-engine.md)
  — app-wide ELK (`elkjs`) auto-layout seam for `apps/aiperf-flow`: replaces
  every diagram's hand-picked `{x,y}` node positions with a measure→layout→apply
  cycle driven by real React Flow node sizes, fixing smooshed boxes and
  doubled-back edges; opt-in via `PipelineCanvas`'s `layout` prop / `AutoLayoutFlow`,
  adopted by `rust-port-flow` first then rolled out to the rest.
- [`docs/specs/2026-07-25-hf-generic-datasets-design.md`](docs/specs/2026-07-25-hf-generic-datasets-design.md)
  — built generic HuggingFace-dataset-by-ID input: a `--hf-dataset <id>` CLI/YAML
  passthrough that bypasses the hard-coded public catalog, plus a source-agnostic
  `hf` composer whose `infer_row_layout` auto-detects prompt/completion fields
  (message-array / flat / `context`+`input`) with explicit overrides and `/info`
  split-config resolution, on top of AIPerf's existing HF transport.

Execution and scheduling:

- [`docs/specs/execution-model.md`](docs/specs/execution-model.md) — the single
  thread-per-core hot path, the two-trait transport seam, worker-local
  accumulation, and the shared reduce/measure layers.
- [`docs/specs/flatgraph-fast-path.md`](docs/specs/flatgraph-fast-path.md) — built
  `FlatGraphActor` fast path: eligible local and worker-backed production graph
  placement routes one-node/no-fan-in traces through the shared sink without the
  general graph context, proven byte-identical to the general executor through the
  real `aiperf` binary; later scheduled-workload and multi-node work remain future.
- [`docs/specs/scheduling.md`](docs/specs/scheduling.md) — request-rate, concurrency,
  user-centric, and fixed-schedule workloads over one `Clock`-backed runtime, and
  how each partitions across sub-cells.
- [`docs/specs/global-exact-dispatch.md`](docs/specs/global-exact-dispatch.md) — the
  built `runtime.dispatch` selector (`sharded` | `global` | `global-hop`)
  replacing the static per-thread partition with a shared per-cell
  `GlobalAdmission` gate (`global`, the `workers>1` default) or a
  single-coordinator hop dispatcher (`global-hop`) so `workers>1` runs are
  byte-exact against Python's single global concurrency/rate limiter.
- [`docs/specs/phase-orchestration.md`](docs/specs/phase-orchestration.md) — one
  `Clock`-native warmup→profiling lifecycle: escalation ladder, cancellation
  latch, and the seam scheduled and graph runs share.
- [`docs/specs/ancillary-timing.md`](docs/specs/ancillary-timing.md) — ramping, seeded
  request cancellation, and sticky round-robin URL selection over a running
  phase.
- [`docs/specs/adaptive-scale.md`](docs/specs/adaptive-scale.md) — the closed-loop SLA
  controller (`ramp_until_fail`), its four live actuators, and its schema-v2
  artifacts.
- [`docs/specs/cellular.md`](docs/specs/cellular.md) — partitioning one run across cell
  processes, the multi-process and velo cross-host topologies, and the fidelity
  guards.
- [`docs/specs/velo-hub.md`](docs/specs/velo-hub.md) — the per-experiment control-plane hub
  (`aiperf_runtime::hub`, `cellular` feature): a plugin trait whose plugins each
  contribute an HTTP router and velo handlers backed by one shared handler
  function, the discovery connect-by-endpoint plugin, and the cell↔controller,
  `/artifact`, `/dataset` (fan-out), and `/phaser` plugins that fold every standalone
  velo plane onto the hub, and the `AIPERF_CELLULAR_HUB` bootstrap toggle in
  `engine::cellular_controller`.
- [`docs/specs/slurm-native.md`](docs/specs/slurm-native.md) — running a cellular benchmark
  natively under a SLURM allocation: the `aiperf slurm run` rank dispatch, the
  `SLURM_*` → controller/cell topology mapping, the `SlurmLauncher`, and the
  `aiperf slurm generate` sbatch generator.

Transports:

- [`docs/specs/http-transport.md`](docs/specs/http-transport.md) — the Clock-injected hyper
  HTTP stack: protocols, SSE streaming, endpoint binding, forward-proxy `CONNECT`
  tunnelling (`--proxy`/`--proxy-from-env`), and post-send cancellation.
- [`docs/specs/grpc-transport.md`](docs/specs/grpc-transport.md) — the Clock-injected Tonic
  gRPC stack: the binding registry, KServe OIP v2 and Riva families, the
  protoc-free codec, and the worker-local sink.
- [`docs/specs/websocket-transport.md`](docs/specs/websocket-transport.md) — built reusable
  content, SSE, bidirectional framing, measurement, placement, and registration
  prerequisites plus the future Clock-injected WebSocket transport contract.
- [`docs/specs/sagemaker-runtime-endpoint.md`](docs/specs/sagemaker-runtime-endpoint.md) —
  AWS SageMaker Runtime dialect: `InvokeEndpoint`/
  `InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream` mock-server routes, the AWS
  `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` binary frame codec, and the
  single-factory client endpoint dialect it composes over, verified e2e and
  against a genuine `boto3` client.
- [`docs/specs/offline-cosimulation.md`](docs/specs/offline-cosimulation.md) — socket-free
  Dynamo co-simulation behind the `dynosim` feature: the steppable clocked engine
  boundary and the observer contract.

Inputs, endpoints, and graph:

- [`docs/specs/dataset.md`](docs/specs/dataset.md) — the content-addressed segment store and
  the loader→compose→store→sampler→materializer pipeline.
- [`docs/specs/prompt-corpus.md`](docs/specs/prompt-corpus.md) — the shared `prompts.corpus`
  seam for synthetic, count/hash-based trace, and recorded-graph prompt synthesis over
  the `sonnet`, `coding`, and exact-length `random` corpora.
- [`docs/specs/endpoint-body-construction.md`](docs/specs/endpoint-body-construction.md) —
  `format_payload → BodyPlan` and the two shared materializers that turn segment
  handles into wire bytes.
- [`docs/specs/endpoints.md`](docs/specs/endpoints.md) — the `Endpoint` dialect adapter, the
  native dialects, endpoint identity, and the registry consumed by validation and
  execution.
- [`docs/specs/content-server.md`](docs/specs/content-server.md) — the run-owned HTTP
  delivery sidecar that serves generated media by URL, its publication seam, and
  request-correlated media-fetch metrics (`rid`/`mi`/`td` URL tagging, streaming
  drain into `SidecarMetric` distributions).
- [`docs/specs/rng.md`](docs/specs/rng.md) — the hash-derived randomness substrate:
  order-independent BLAKE3 stream derivation, generators, and sampling
  distributions.
- [`docs/specs/graph-runtime.md`](docs/specs/graph-runtime.md) — the Graph-IR runtime:
  deterministic async dataflow, the recorded-trace compilers, and the
  trajectory-snapshot/warmup-priming subsystem.
- [`docs/specs/graph-ir-system-idle-gap.md`](docs/specs/graph-ir-system-idle-gap.md) — Graph-IR system idle-gap cap at the centralized node firing gate.
- [`docs/specs/conditional-graph-lowering.md`](docs/specs/conditional-graph-lowering.md) —
  the model-independent-branching contract: pinned/recorded/weighted conditional
  branching and recorded non-LLM content resolved and folded into the flat
  `LlmNode`/`StaticEdge` substrate at lowering, the eager-vs-forbidden
  (branch-on-live-output) line, and the built `conditional_graph` eager-conditional
  compiler (`rust/runtime/src/graph/conditional/`).
- [`docs/specs/agentx-rust-port.md`](docs/specs/agentx-rust-port.md) — the standalone,
  always-compiled byte-exact Rust port of the Python AgentX (WEKA replay +
  agentic-replay timing + scenario locks); parallel to and switchable against
  graph-ir via `--weka-semantics`, proven by raw-export A/B parity under SimClock.
  Transitional (`rust/runtime/src/agentx/`), deleted once graph-ir supersedes it.
- [`docs/specs/agentic-replay-join-gating.md`](docs/specs/agentic-replay-join-gating.md) —
  forward-looking design record for cross-lane subagent spawn/join gating and
  tree-gated recycle in the `agentic_replay` timing mode (`rust/runtime/src/agentic_replay.rs`),
  the remaining byte-exact-parity piece for subagent trajectory trees, driven by the
  ported `agentx::session_tree` registry over `Turn.prerequisites`/`ConversationBranch`.
- [`docs/specs/agentic-accelerated-cache-warmup.md`](docs/specs/agentic-accelerated-cache-warmup.md) —
  the gated accelerated cache-pressure warmup + warmup→profiling residual-delay handoff
  in the legacy `agentic_replay` timing mode (`--agentic-cache-warmup-duration`); the
  terminal parity subsystem (built; residual/handoff golden-verified against the real
  Python methods, live global-hop clean on `weka_cc_traces_062126`), mining the graph
  path's Clock-derived `chop_trie_at_frontier`/`GraphWarmupHandoff` reference.
- [`docs/specs/global-hop-worker-routing.md`](docs/specs/global-hop-worker-routing.md) —
  forward-looking design record for pluggable worker-assignment routing in the
  multi-worker `global-hop` dispatcher (`--hop-routing round-robin|sticky|least-loaded`,
  applied at `ThreadPerCoreExecutor::execute_command`); makes `StickyUserSessions`
  connection reuse honored per session (hash-by-correlation) instead of fragmented,
  auto-defaulting to sticky under sticky reuse.

Measurement and output:

- [`docs/specs/metrics.md`](docs/specs/metrics.md) — the IO-free metrics engine: the
  column-store accumulator, the metric catalog, sweep curves, and the typed
  report; exact vs sketch modes.
- [`docs/specs/definition-registry.md`](docs/specs/definition-registry.md) — built
  single shared definition layer: a lookup-only `Definition` (header, units,
  `larger_is_better`, `value_type`, group, order) for metrics and dataset-analysis
  outputs (server/GPU telemetry still seam-only), split out of `MetricSpec`, keyed by
  namespaced id, made compile-time complete via the const-array `[MetricSpec; COUNT]`
  length, and used for SLA comparison, table rendering, and the `aiperf metrics`
  command.
- [`docs/specs/telemetry.md`](docs/specs/telemetry.md) — GPU telemetry, server metrics, and
  network latency side channels feeding the metrics seam.
- [`docs/specs/exporters.md`](docs/specs/exporters.md) — the typed report core and the
  static set of `Exporter` sinks behind one trait.
- [`docs/specs/accuracy.md`](docs/specs/accuracy.md) — the Rust dispatch/capture vs
  pinned-Python grading split, the injected evaluator seam, and sharded capture
  with a single grade.
- [`docs/specs/dataset-analysis.md`](docs/specs/dataset-analysis.md) — built `--dry-run`
  analytical report: dataset shape, turn-by-turn ISL/OSL, prefix/KV-cache reuse
  (ideal and finite-capacity), and the real execution timeline distilled from a
  dry run's records, emitted as `dataset_analysis.{txt,json,csv,html}`.

Targets:

- [`docs/specs/mock-server.md`](docs/specs/mock-server.md) — the standalone HTTP/gRPC
  inference target with deterministic generation, latency and error models,
  telemetry, and request recording.

## Build / test / run

Use `cargo build --release`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and
`cargo fmt` for Rust development. Build the feature-bearing `aiperf` binary with
`cargo build -p aiperf-cli --features dynosim`. Package the **single `aiperf`
wheel** (maturin backend, root `pyproject.toml`) with `make wheel`:
`make bundle-cli` builds the full-fat unified `aiperf` binary (`lto=fat`, crate
default `--features full`); `maturin build` emits one platform-specific wheel
carrying the `pyext` `aiperf._native` module and the `src/aiperf` frontend; and
`tools/wheel_repack.py` then repacks the binary directly into the wheel's scripts
directory as `aiperf-<ver>.data/scripts/aiperf` — no separate
`aiperf`/`aiperf_rust` wheel. The installed `aiperf` command IS the native
binary. End users run `aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml`; the pure-Python
frontend is reachable as `aiperf-python` and `python -m aiperf`.
`cargo run -p aiperf-runtime` and native `--offline`/mode flags do not exist.
